Weekly Dish: Incontro Moving to Danville
Incontro Ristorante moving to Danville; savory waffle sandwiches at La Boulange in Walnut Creek; Tender Greens and Toast open; taco taste-off in Oakland; and more in this week's Dish!
By Ethan Fletcher May 2, 2011 
Photo by Cody Pickens

Three time Diablo Food Award winner Incontro Ristorante will be moving from San Ramon to a larger location in downtown Danville according to co-owner Gianni Bartoletti. The authentic rustic Italian eatery that has drawn in diners despite its out-of-the-way location in a nondescript section of San Ramon is taking over La Ultima, which will be closing after more than 30 years dishing out comforting Mexican food on Hartz Avenue. (CLICK HERE to read a nice article on La Ultima in the Contra Costa Times over the weekend)

For Bartoletti, the move was a natural, and he's clearly looking forward to the benefits the new downtown location will bring: increased foot traffic, a larger location that can accommodate more diners, a planned outdoor patio, as well as eventually a full bar (his San Ramon location was beer and wine only). But despite those changes, Bartoletti says he wants to keep most everything the same, especially the food, which includes weekly changing specials.

"Basically what we’re going to do is move Incontro from this location to there, nothing more, nothing less," he says. "There’s no secret, our formula has always been the same: good service, good product, friendly atmosphere, it’s as simple as that. We'll have a full page of specials that always change—my restaurant is never be boring, you'll always discover something new."

Bartoletti and fellow co-owner Stefano Giovacchini plan an extensive renovation of the La Ultima location on 455 Hartz Avenue, including turning the outdoor patio into an "Italian veranda" with lighted trees, fire pits, and an Italian fountain. There will be a happy hour, and they plan to be open eventually for lunch as well as dinner. Bartoletti says he is hoping (he admits, ambitiously) to open by August in time to capture some summer business. He'll be bringing most of his staff with him, including his executive chef Raul Aguirre. And while Bartoletti said he is sorry to be leaving San Ramon, he is happy to be moving to a more central location that is still in the Tri-Valley area where he has built up a loyal clientele.

"You know, we went through the 2009 recession, and if it weren't for our loyal local customers we wouldn't still be here,' he says. "We wanted to be more exposed, to be even more a part of the community—I think Incontro is going to be a really good fit for Danville."

I had a chance to speak with La Boulange owner Pascal Rigo who gave me a few more details on the new La Boulange that is taking over one half of the Bing Crosby's space in Walnut Creek. The French-born Rigo, baked bread all over the country, including Bordeaux and Paris before moving to San Francisco 17 years ago, told me that the new Walnut Creek location (which he hoped to open by November) would actually be a little different from his other cafes.He said that the new La Boulange would be offering four daily specials in addition to its usual selection of soups, pastries, sandwiches and salads. He also said Walnut Creek would serve as the guinea pig for the debut of a new savory waffle sandwich that he promised would be "super crispy and light."

Sounds good to me. Rigo also said be hoped to offer yogurt smoothies (called Le Frappe, of course), and that he is excited to move into Walnut Creek after recently opening locations in Danville and Lafayette.No word yet on whether the new spot will be painted green, purple, or blue but Rigo said they might let people vote for their favorite choice online. We'll keep you posted...

Opening alert, and no it's not Home of Chicken and Waffles... Tender Greens debuted over the weekend on Locust Street in downtown Walnut Creek. I went down to check it out on Monday and came away impressed. I got a Cobb salad (not the most adventurous option I know, but it was very tasty) and checked out the menu: there's a range of "big salads" for $10.50, some "hot stuff" including marinated steak, salt and pepper chicken, and herb brushed local albacore. It's a nice spot too, with a pretty interior (including reclaimed materials) and plenty of outdoor seating. They carry local beers and wines, Weaver's coffee (brewed in San Rafael by former Peet's master roaster John Weaver), and a delicious looking selection of housemade pastries (including homemade pop tarts). They'll also be doing three or four rotating specials for dinner. 1352 Locust Street, Walnut Creek, (925) 937-5100,

Also open is Toast Wine Lounge in Rockridge. Haven't been here yet, but their menu looks pretty mouth-watering: burrata and fennel pollen with olive relish on toast; wild-caught chilled shrimp salad with baby lettuces, youkon gold potatoes and Romesco sauce; braised Piedmontese beef short rib with butternut squash puree. Nice! The chef is Peter Jackson who has, according to the website, worked with several well-known Bay Area chefs including Bradley Ogden and for the last five years has been working on "the cutting edge of the underground food movement," including running a food cart with cured meats and gumbo. Toast's food will focus on wine country cuisine; seasonal, local, sustainable of course.

Toast Wine Lounge, 5900 College Ave., Oakland, (510) 586-5900, toastwinelounge.com/
